forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329110006_654a633e
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r, j be integers with 0 <= a <= b, r >= 0, and 0 <= j <= floor(r (b - a) / 2). Put I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}. For each positive integer d, define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|, and assume M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d. Let X_j be the set of pairs (S, lambda) such that S is a subset of I, lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I, |lambda| denotes the sum of the elements of lambda, and |lambda| + sum_{s in S} (r + s) = j. Then there exists an involution iota_j : X_j -> X_j such that: (1) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S',lambda') != (S,lambda), then |S'| is congruent to |S| + 1 modulo 2; and (2) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S,lambda), then |S| is even.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329092547_6a64d34a
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: For integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, let q be an indeterminate, define (q;q)_n := product_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j) for n >= 0 with (q;q)_0 := 1, set R_{a,b,r}(q) := ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b), and define D := r (b - a). Assume that R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q]. Then for every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), the coefficient of q^j in R_{a,b,r}(q) is a nonnegative integer.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329074016_d9949d95
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with empty product equal to 1. Assume that for every positive integer d one has floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d). Then P_{a,b,r}(q) is a polynomial in Z[q], and every coefficient of P_{a,b,r}(q) is nonnegative.

payload.statement_nl:
Let a, b, r, j be integers with 0 <= a <= b, r >= 0, and j >= 0. Set I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}. Define X_j to be the set of all pairs (S, lambda) such that S is a subset of I, lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I, and wt(lambda) + sum_{s in S}(r+s) = j, where wt(lambda) is the sum of the elements of lambda. Then X_j is finite. If E_j is the number of elements (S,lambda) in X_j with |S| even and O_j is the number of elements (S,lambda) in X_j with |S| odd, then
sum_{(S,lambda) in X_j} (-1)^{|S|} = E_j - O_j.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Since 0 <= a <= b, the set I = {a+1, a+2, ..., b} has exactly b-a elements, so I is finite. Hence there are only finitely many subsets S of I, in fact exactly 2^(b-a) of them.

Fix one such subset S. Suppose (S, lambda) is in X_j. For each t in I, let m_t be the multiplicity of t in the finite multiset lambda. Because I is finite, the multiset lambda is uniquely determined by the tuple (m_t) indexed by t in I. Also,
wt(lambda) = sum_{t in I} t m_t = j - sum_{s in S}(r+s).
Now r >= 0, and every s in I satisfies s >= a+1 >= 1, so each term r+s is nonnegative. Therefore sum_{s in S}(r+s) >= 0, and hence wt(lambda) <= j.

For each t in I we have t >= 1, so
0 <= m_t <= t m_t <= sum_{u in I} u m_u = wt(lambda) <= j.
Thus each m_t is an integer in {0,1,...,j}. Since I has b-a elements, there are at most (j+1)^(b-a) possible tuples (m_t), and therefore at most (j+1)^(b-a) possible multisets lambda for this fixed S. Since there are only finitely many choices of S, we obtain
|X_j| <= 2^(b-a) (j+1)^(b-a) < infinity.
So X_j is finite.

Now define
X_j^even = {(S, lambda) in X_j : |S| is even}
and
X_j^odd = {(S, lambda) in X_j : |S| is odd}.
These two sets are disjoint and their union is X_j. By the definitions of E_j and O_j, we have |X_j^even| = E_j and |X_j^odd| = O_j.

Because X_j is finite, we may split the finite sum over X_j according to this partition:
sum_{(S,lambda) in X_j} (-1)^{|S|}
= sum_{(S,lambda) in X_j^even} (-1)^{|S|} + sum_{(S,lambda) in X_j^odd} (-1)^{|S|}.
If (S,lambda) lies in X_j^even, then (-1)^{|S|} = 1. If (S,lambda) lies in X_j^odd, then (-1)^{|S|} = -1. Hence
sum_{(S,lambda) in X_j} (-1)^{|S|}
= sum_{(S,lambda) in X_j^even} 1 + sum_{(S,lambda) in X_j^odd} (-1)
= |X_j^even| - |X_j^odd|
= E_j - O_j.
This is exactly the claimed identity.
result_payload.proof_summary: I is finite, and for any admissible pair (S, lambda), the weight of lambda is at most j. Since every element of I is at least 1, each multiplicity in lambda is at most j, so only finitely many multisets lambda can occur; combined with finitely many subsets S, this makes X_j finite. Then partition X_j into the elements with |S| even and odd; the summand is 1 on the even part and -1 on the odd part, so the total sum is E_j - O_j.
